findings.description: The KMS key does not enable automatic key rotation (enable_key_rotation is absent, defaulting to false), so the same key material can be used indefinitely for encrypting the audit bucket. Long-lived keys increase the blast radius of a key compromise and violate CIS/AWS best practice for customer-managed keys.

deletion_window_in_days = 7 sets the minimum allowed window, so the audit-trail key can be scheduled for destruction and irreversibly deleted only 7 days later. A shorter window reduces the time to detect and cancel an unauthorized or accidental key deletion, which would render audit log data unrecoverable.

No aws_kms_key_policy is attached to the key (nor an inline policy), so the key relies on the default permissive policy, which grants the AWS account root principal full control over the key. Any principal in the account with kms:* permissions can manage, disable, or delete this audit-trail key, weakening protection of the audit data it encrypts.
